clue.text: Carries family's headgear

parts.note: to carry a load is to bear it, so carries gives bears
kin means family or relatives; the possessive adds nothing

explanation.surface: Someone carries off the family's prized hats.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEARSKIN is the tall fur cap worn by British guardsmen outside Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall fur cap of the Guards regiments is a type of military hat.

clue.text: Pub's current wine

parts.note: a pub is a bar; the possessive gives the S
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A pub serves the wine currently in fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white Bordeaux from a village of the same name.

clue.text: Set out on a donkey to get to your property

indicators.note: in a down answer, the rearranged letters sit on top of the donkey word, after it

parts.note: an ass is a donkey

indicators.note: out signals the letters of Set are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone sets off riding a donkey to reach their land.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are the things of value someone owns.

clue.text: Spanish drink has fermentation of grain in it

indicators.note: in it puts the rearranged letters inside the word for it

parts.note: SA, sex appeal, is crossword shorthand for it

indicators.note: fermentation stirs things up, so the letters of grain are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Spanish drink contains fermented grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal (SA) is an old convention; the fermented grain becomes ANGRI inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish punch of red wine and fruit.

clue.text: I dry up dessert dishes

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for dry is read bottom to top

parts.note: sec is French for dry, used of wine

explanation.surface: Someone dries the pudding bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: Ices are frozen sweets served as puddings.

clue.text: Go up like many at last

parts.note: as means like, in the sense of in the manner of
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a crossword stand-in for many
an end is what comes at last, the final point

explanation.surface: A crowd finally climbs upward together.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb or rise is a plain synonym for going up.

clue.text: Pull out of reach

explanation.definitionFit: Extending by pulling and an unbroken extent share the word.

clue.text: Fabulous opportunities here for outcast loaded with gold

indicators.note: loaded with gold puts the gold word inside the rearranged letters
outcast suggests something thrown out of place, so the letters of loaded are rearranged

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: An exile laden with treasure seeks a land of fabulous fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' acts as a container signal here: being loaded with something means holding it, so the gold sits inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado is the legendary city of gold, a byword for a place of riches.

clue.text: Training horses to cover land with manure, over a period of time

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first word above the second

parts.note: to dress soil is to spread manure or fertiliser on it
an age is a long period

explanation.surface: A farmer manures the field over a season while schooling horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the formal schooling of horses in precise movements.

clue.text: Didn't like being despatched in a pipe

indicators.note: the despatched word sits in the pipe word, signalling a container

parts.note: a reed is a hollow stem or a musical pipe
despatched means sent off

explanation.surface: Someone resented being posted inside a pipe like a message.
explanation.definitionFit: To take offence at something is to dislike it bitterly.

clue.text: Card game one may come across

definitions.meaning: a trick-taking card game for four players in pairs
a structure spanning a river, which one walks across

explanation.definitionFit: The partnership card game and a span over a river or road share the name.

clue.text: Cast out Croats

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of Croats are put out of order

explanation.surface: A group of Croatian people is expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast out' reads as one verb meaning expel; split it, and Cast is the definition while 'out' rearranges Croats.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast of a play is its company of performers.

clue.text: True luv's turned out to be one of these flappers?

indicators.note: turned out suggests a reworking, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A genuine sweetheart is revealed as one of those flighty young women of the 1920s.
explanation.walkthrough: Flappers suggests the jazz-age girls; here it means big birds flapping their wings.
explanation.definitionFit: Large carrion birds flap broad wings, so they are whimsically called flappers.

clue.text: Middle-age — a classification that's causing irritation

indicators.note: middle picks the central letter of the word age

parts.note: a rating is a classification or grade

explanation.surface: Middle age gets its own category, which is annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating noise or manner rasps on the nerves.

clue.text: A little bit of chow recommended if you've a hangover?

definitions.text: A little bit of chow recommended if you've a hangover?

parts.words: A little bit of chow recommended if you've a hangover?
parts.note: the phrase for a morning drink to cure a hangover is read literally as a tuft of fur from a chow, a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Advice to eat a snack after a night of heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a small drink taken to ease a hangover, literally a tuft from a dog.

clue.text: Dashed on getting first serving cooked in spices

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of serving

parts.note: curried food is cooked with hot spices

explanation.surface: Someone rushes off after the first helping of spicy food.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry is to run with quick short steps, so to hurry.

clue.text: Following the ringleader inside and leaving nothing to chance

indicators.note: inside puts the leader's letter within the word for following

parts.note: ensuing means following

indicators.note: the leader of ring is its first letter

explanation.surface: Coming after the gang boss, someone makes sure nothing goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringleader' must be split: 'leader' takes the first letter of 'ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensuring means making certain, guaranteeing an outcome.

clue.text: A normal habit for nuns dwelling on Scottish isle, by lake

parts.note: a convent is the dwelling for a community of nuns
Iona is a small island of the Inner Hebrides, off western Scotland
L is the standard abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Nuns living on a Hebridean island beside a loch keep an ordinary routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A normal habit' tempts one to look for a nun's garment; 'A' and 'habit' are only surface padding and 'on' and 'by' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something conventional follows accepted custom, so it is ordinary.

clue.text: Puzzles turning up in duplicate with a trap in them

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the whole assembly bottom to top
in them puts the trap word inside the duplicate word

parts.note: same means identical, a duplicate
a gin is a snare or trap

explanation.surface: Riddles keep surfacing in twin copies with a snare inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' applies to the whole assembly, so the trap goes inside the duplicate first and only then is everything read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmas are riddles or baffling problems.

clue.text: A scholar with energy that's mind-boggling

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar
zing means vitality or energy

explanation.surface: A lively academic proves astonishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing means astonishing, beyond belief.

clue.text: Bad mark

parts.note: read as a mark of disgrace on someone's reputation rather than a poor grade

explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to a person.

clue.text: Right of admission to the course

definitions.meaning: the freedom to enter a place or circle
a dish of a meal, usually the main one

explanation.definitionFit: Entrée means both the privilege of entry and a dish served in a meal.

clue.text: Meeting after separation leading to one's ruin

indicators.note: leading to suggests one thing turning into another, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its S, as the letters ONES
taken as written

explanation.surface: A break-up followed by getting back together brings someone to disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is singular while the answer is plural; the clue as printed may have read 'Meetings'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatherings of people who have been apart, such as old classmates.

clue.text: Bar cricketer rejecting net

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

indicators.note: rejecting suggests throwing back, so the word net is read backwards

explanation.surface: A batsman refuses to practise in the nets.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bat is a batsman and the nets are the practice cages.
explanation.definitionFit: A batten is a long strip of wood, a kind of bar.

clue.text: A piano piece? Capital!

indicators.note: piece signals a part taken from within the words A piano

explanation.surface: Someone praises a piano work as excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' looks like an exclamation of approval; it defines the capital city of Samoa.
explanation.definitionFit: Apia is the capital city of Samoa in the Pacific.

clue.text: Lidless lid? I'm so confused by these peculiarities of language

indicators.note: lidless means the word lid loses its top, its first letter
confused signals the letters of I'm so are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written, letters IMSO

explanation.surface: A muddled person babbles about a lid that has no lid.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressions whose meaning is particular to one tongue are its quirks of usage.

clue.text: Spaniel seen to leap at the Queen

parts.note: to spring is to leap
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A dog is spotted jumping at the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is a breed of gundog in the spaniel family.

clue.text: Summary way to dispose of a meal

definitions.text: way to dispose of a meal
definitions.meaning: to process food in the stomach

explanation.definitionFit: A condensed summary and the body's processing of food share the word.

clue.text: Desecrate tomb of foreign nobleman

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or deface
a grave is a tomb

explanation.surface: A vandal defiles the burial place of a foreign aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A margrave was a German count ruling a border province.
